obs: tin calcined in an open crucible weighs somewhat more afterward, the crucible having stood uncovered among the soot and ash of the furnace
two pieces of ice rubbed together are found to melt at the rubbing faces, the trial being made in a warm room with the bare hands
one flask of broth, boiled and corked, stays clear for a week, the others prepared with it having spoiled
a visiting physician reports that in one street the cholera seemed lighter among those who drank from a certain well, no count of the houses having been made
the planet Venus appears to the naked eye somewhat brighter at some seasons than at others
two stones of unequal weight thrown by hand from a wall are judged by the bystanders to strike the ground nearly together
a certain well pump, old and leaky in its leathers, fails to raise water above thirty feet
a hair held before a candle is said by one observer to cast a shadow with faintly coloured edges, seen once with the unaided eye
a substance resembling urea is obtained in the laboratory from a preparation of which a part was drawn from animal charcoal
two varieties of pigeon bred by fanciers differ somewhat in the feathers of the tail
one patient with pneumonia who refused the lancet recovered
the place of Mars taken on one night with a small quadrant differs by ten minutes of arc from the tables
sailors report a bright light seen for one night low in the sky, which no astronomer found again
a butcher remarks that a slaughtered ox yields more blood than he had looked for
a dew gathers upon the inside of a cold glass held over a burning lamp in a damp room
a traveller describes a cliff of clay some hundreds of feet high and supposes it must have taken long to gather
a single block of basalt lies near a hill which the peasants say once smoked
in one month the ward served by students lost more women than the ward served by midwives, and in another month fewer
one scorbutic seaman who ate apples on reaching port mended within a fortnight, as did his messmates who went ashore with him
the compass of a ship is found disordered after a thunderstorm in which the vessel was struck and much shaken
one eclipse of a satellite of Jupiter came some minutes late by the clock of a single observer, which was compared with no other
a peasant brings a blackened stone which he says fell in his field during a storm, no other person having seen it fall
one boulder among many is found to bear scratches upon one side
potash heated strongly in an iron tube leaves a grey residue, the tube itself being found corroded
a single trial with heated iron fails to draw oxygen from muriatic acid
a traveller remarks that gnats are plentiful in the districts where the ague prevails
one observer, timing the flash and report of a single gun with a pocket watch, makes the speed somewhat greater than the calculation
a comet is observed at a distance from the sun that fits no term of the progression
one analysis gives the atomic weight of chlorine as 35.4, the silver used not having been purified
a dog whose tail was docked sired one litter of pups with tails
a physician pressing upon the arm of a patient judges the muscle no larger when it is clenched
a traveller's clock is found slow on arrival in the tropics after a rough voyage of two months

the planet Uranus departs from its computed place by more than a minute of arc, three other planets err in the same manner, and no disturbing body is found where the errors point, though sought for fifty years with the largest telescopes
the comet returns neither at the time computed nor within ten years after, though the pull of Jupiter and Saturn is fully reckoned by three computers and the sky is watched nightly
astronomers report that instruments proved able to show the yearly shift of a star a million times farther off than the sun show none whatever in a thousand stars
the motion of the moon's apogee, carried to every further term of the series by three geometers separately, still comes out only half of what is observed
Sirius and a hundred other stars move in wavy lines across the sky, and the largest telescopes and the spectroscope find nothing of any mass near one of them
when two balls of soft lead collide and stop dead, the most delicate thermometers show no warmth in them, and no change of shape, sound or motion is found in anything about them
a log burnt in a sealed glass vessel upon the balance, with all its smoke and airs retained, weighs sensibly less after burning than before, at every repetition
many experimenters report that gravy boiled for an hour in flasks sealed by melting the glass itself swarms with animalcules within days
patients blindfolded and not told when the magnetiser's hand approaches fall into convulsions exactly when it does and never when they are told so falsely, before a royal commission
a committee of physicists reports that tables travel across the room while the sitters' hands rest upon cards that slip freely on rollers, and while no hand touches them at all
nitrogen drawn from the air, freed from every other substance that chemistry or the spectroscope can detect, remains heavier by one part in two hundred than nitrogen prepared from ammonia
the atomic weight of indium, determined afresh by its specific heat and by several chemists, stays at 75.6, and a dozen other elements likewise fall where their properties do not belong
the vapour of sal-ammoniac has but half the density its formula requires, is proved by diffusion to be a single unbroken gas, and a great many other vapours behave likewise
water distilled in vessels of gold and platinum, which lose no weight, leaves each time an earthy sediment, and the water is lighter by exactly so much
a commission of engineers reports that a machine which they took to pieces, examined, and set up again in a sealed room of their own choosing ran for a year and raised weights without ceasing
the gain of Jupiter and the loss of Saturn, with every mutual attraction computed to the last term, remain wholly unaccounted for and go on in one direction through twenty centuries of records
solutions of sugar and of every other substance tried, salts and others alike, press by amounts that bear no relation to the number of their molecules
when a small round disc is set in a beam of light and the centre of its shadow is examined, it is found perfectly dark, in the trials of several opticians
under the microscope, in the lung of the frog and the web of its foot, the arteries are seen to end blindly, and coloured fluid driven into the arteries never reaches the veins
a heavy pendulum hung from a high dome keeps its plane of swing unchanged with respect to the floor through a whole day, at Paris and at every other place where it is tried
physicians of several cities report that the bacillus is found as often in the healthy as in the sick, and a hundred persons who swallow full cultures all remain well
a vessel closed against every exchange of heat and holding only water grows steadily warmer year after year, in the hands of many observers
in formations searched bed by bed over whole continents, all the species appear together in the lowest strata, man beside the trilobite, with no succession whatever
when counts are made in several cities, the vaccinated take the small-pox as often and die of it as often as the unvaccinated, at every age and every interval from vaccination
